1.definition: An Alid is a descendant of Ali ibn Abi Talib — the Prophet Muhammad's cousin and son-in-law — and his wife Fatima, the Prophet's daughter. Because they carried the Prophet's bloodline, Alids were a magnet for opposition movements that argued the caliphate rightfully belonged to Muhammad's family rather than to the Umayyads or Abbasids. The Shia tradition grew up around their claim.

Arabic for 'the Second Great Sedition' — the four-year civil war (811–813) that broke out between Harun al-Rashid's sons al-Amin and al-Ma'mun after his death. The name distinguishes it from the first great fitna, the seventh-century civil war that produced the Sunni-Shia split. It ended with Baghdad besieged and breached and al-Amin beheaded by his brother's Iranian army.

2.definition: Hubaysh ibn al-Hasan al-Dimashqi was a nephew and pupil of the great translator Hunayn ibn Ishaq, and one of the most productive members of Hunayn's translation school in ninth-century Baghdad. He turned Greek medical and scientific works into Arabic, often revising or completing translations begun by his uncle.

3.definition: The 'Treatise on Decoding Cryptographic Messages,' written by the 9th-century philosopher al-Kindi. It is the earliest known systematic account of frequency analysis — breaking a cipher by counting how often each letter appears — and so is regarded as the founding work of codebreaking as a discipline.

4.definition: Al-Razi's treatise "On Smallpox and Measles" (c. 900), the first work to clearly distinguish the two diseases from each other and to describe the symptoms and course of each in clinical detail. It was translated repeatedly into Latin and other European languages and is considered a masterpiece of early clinical observation.

The Egyptian physician who in 1924 found the lost Arabic manuscript of Ibn al-Nafis in the Prussian State Library in Berlin and recognized that it described pulmonary circulation three centuries before European medicine did. His rediscovery rewrote the history of one of medicine's foundational findings.

5.definition: Al-Ghazali's partial spiritual autobiography (c. 1108), whose title means "Deliverance from Error." In it he describes the crisis of doubt that drove him from his Baghdad professorship into a decade of Sufi wandering, and lays out his search for certain knowledge through theology, philosophy, Ismaili authority, and finally mysticism.

6.definition: Qahir al-Falak ("Conqueror of the Heavens") was the medieval Arabic name for the planet Mars. Fatimid court astrologers timed the founding of their new capital to coincide with the moment Mars was rising, and named the city al-Qahira ("the Victorious," modern Cairo) after the planet — a reminder of how seriously these courts took astrology as a tool of statecraft.
